text:
A state with lifetime \(\tau\) has a natural energy width of order

\[
\Delta E \sim \frac{\hbar}{\tau}.
\]

Using \(\hbar=6.58\times10^{-16}\,\text{eV·s}\),

\[
\Delta E_1\sim \frac{6.58\times10^{-16}}{10^{-9}}
=6.6\times10^{-7}\,\text{eV},
\]

\[
\Delta E_2\sim \frac{6.58\times10^{-16}}{10^{-8}}
=6.6\times10^{-8}\,\text{eV}.
\]

Thus, the combined linewidth is roughly \(7\times10^{-7}\,\text{eV}\). The shorter-lived state dominates the resolution limit. The energy separation must therefore be substantially larger than this. Among the options, only

\[
10^{-4}\,\text{eV}
\]

is clearly much larger than the linewidths.

Answer: B
